beats.say: Their demo exposed private project details, a relocation plan, and a salary figure.
And it wasn't a bug in the GitHub server. The researchers called it an architectural problem, so there's no simple patch.

vis.sub: the agent can't tell data from instructions

beats.say: Give your agent the least access it needs. One repo per session, and a token that can't read your private code.
Here's the prompt. Screenshot it, and send it to Claude inside your project.
Follow Ship With Pip for one of these every day.

prompt: Review how this agent is allowed to use GitHub. List every token and MCP server it can reach, and which private repos each one can read. Propose the minimum setup: a fine-grained token limited to one repo, read-only wherever possible, and no write access to public repos. Then write a short checklist of tool calls I should always approve manually.
caption: In May 2025, Invariant Labs showed a malicious GitHub issue could hijack an AI agent (Claude Desktop with the GitHub MCP server) into pulling data from private repos and posting it in a public pull request. They call it an architectural problem, not a server bug. Limit what your agent can reach: one repo per session, scoped tokens, manual approval. The prompt is at the end.
sources: Invariant Labs, 'GitHub MCP Exploited' (May 26 2025): malicious issue in public repo; Claude Desktop + GitHub MCP + Claude 4 Opus; private repo data posted in public PR; architectural issue, not a server bug; mitigations: least privilege, monitoring
Issue text and chat bubble are illustrations of the attack pattern, not the researchers' verbatim text
